title: Philadelphia science museum closes as supporters seek a way back
summary:
A Philadelphia museum that has introduced generations of children to dinosaurs and nature has closed to visitors. Families crowded into the Academy of Natural Sciences Museum during its final weeks in September.

The Academy was founded in 1812 and opened to the public in 1828. In 1868, it became the first place in the world to display a dinosaur skeleton. Its exhibits also included live animals and scenes showing mammals in their habitats.

Drexel University took financial responsibility for the Academy in 2011. The university says costs rose and visitor numbers fell after the pandemic. The museum had already reduced its hours and cancelled its 2026 summer camp.

Supporters want to bring it back. A petition to keep the museum open gathered more than 114,000 signatures. Shortly before the September 30 closing date, the William Penn Foundation offered funding for one year. This temporary help could provide time to seek a lasting solution.

Drexel says it is exploring that offer, but reopening would need a plan to support the museum over time. Philadelphia's city council also plans public hearings to examine the closure and possible solutions.

The Academy holds more than 19 million scientific specimens, or samples used for study. Drexel says students and researchers will keep access to the collection. Public access remains unclear.
why_it_matters: The closure affects a place where children learned about dinosaurs and nature. Reopening and future public access remain uncertain.
